name: Question 10
problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(t),$ where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x=2\pi $ and velocity $v=4$ when $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t.$
worked_solution:
We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\text{d}t \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(\frac{\pi }{2})=4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+C \\ 4 & =2(1)+C \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So the velocity is given by $v(t)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+2.$

Now, we integrate the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+2)\text{d}t \\  & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+2t+K\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $K,$ we use the fact that $x(\frac{\pi }{2})=2\pi .$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2\pi  & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+2(\frac{\pi }{2})+K \\ 2\pi  & =-2(0)+\pi +K \\ K & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+2t+\pi .
$$

Question 10
?

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration a(t)=2cos⁡(t), where t≥0 is the time. If the particle has position x=2π and velocity v=4 when t=π2, calculate the position x of the particle at time t.

a
x(t)=2cos⁡(t)−2t+3π
b
x(t)=−2cos⁡(t)+2t+π
c
x(t)=2sin⁡(t)+2t
d
x(t)=−2cos⁡(t)+4t
e
x(t)=−2sin⁡(t)+2t+π
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity v(t):

v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫2cos⁡(t)dt=2sin⁡(t)+C

To determine C, we use the fact that v(π2)=4. Substituting this into the above gives

4=2sin⁡(π2)+C4=2(1)+CC=2.

So the velocity is given by v(t)=2sin⁡(t)+2.

Now, we integrate the velocity to get x(t):

x(t)=∫v(t)dt=∫(2sin⁡(t)+2)dt=−2cos⁡(t)+2t+K

To determine K, we use the fact that x(π2)=2π. Substituting this into the above gives

2π=−2cos⁡(π2)+2(π2)+K2π=−2(0)+π+KK=π.

Therefore, the position x of the particle at time t is x(t)=−2cos⁡(t)+2t+π.
